description: SDK-only reference vectors and lifecycle COVERAGE MANIFEST; lifecycle entries require native executable tests. Fake credential strings; no AHP wire-schema change. In token_responses, requested is the caller's current requested set, always within allowed (requested scopes outside the ceiling are invalid_configuration); a response scope that is absent, null or blank inherits like an omitted one; wire_request, present for exchange reacquire, is the scope set actually sent: previous_granted plus ceiling-filtered requested and required. keys use client_identity (preregistered:id, cimd:url or dcr), never an issued client_id; registration_keys are client-credentials only; client_selection inputs describe host configuration and authorization-server metadata; registration_responses use now as the current Unix time. scope_decisions and completions fields, and the optional requires features (token_validation_callback, complete_handle, legacy_prepare_time_host_required), are defined in spec/draft/sdk-auth-lifecycle.md (Executable coverage); every defined field must be asserted and an unknown field fails the run. In token_responses, error_scopes is the scope set carried by access_denied.

lifecycle.expect: valid stored grant works without metadata HTTP, including a recreated provider
known authorized binding sends stored token on first attempt; no 401/replay for upload or notification
401/insufficient_scope on a notification or upload is not replayed but runs challenge handling (discovery, client-credentials acquisition, no login creation); the next operation sends a credential
401 for a stored token with unknown or future expiry retires it before any other decision and renews it, so the next operation does not resend the rejected token
up-front lookup never creates a pending login or performs protected-resource discovery; only a store miss or host policy refusal sends an anonymous attempt
up-front lookup refreshes an expired stored token non-interactively using cached authorization-server metadata
expired client-credentials token without refresh token is re-acquired non-interactively by the up-front lookup using persisted metadata
binding record lacking persisted authorization-server metadata fetches only the stored issuer's metadata, never protected-resource metadata; failure is discovery_failed

renewal failing before the token endpoint processed it (DNS, TCP connect, TLS handshake, token-endpoint 404/410) refetches the stored issuer's metadata once, persists it if the issuer is unchanged and retries once; changed issuer or failed refetch is discovery_failed

read timeout, reset after send, 5xx, non-OAuth body or OAuth error during renewal returns its error (provider_failed/retry for ambiguous failures) with no metadata refetch and no immediate retry; the presented refresh token is not replayed
known binding whose non-interactive refresh fails (transient, invalid_grant, missing cached metadata) fails the operation with that error, never sends anonymously
known PKCE binding whose tokens were dropped fails interaction_required at lookup; a later prepare restores it
rotated refresh credential persisted and reusable when expires_in absent
5xx/non-OAuth/timeout retains credentials and returns retry, never permanent fabricated login state
definitive interactive refresh invalid_grant removes access and refresh tokens when the record still holds the presented refresh token, and returns refresh_rejected
invalid_grant for a refresh token already replaced by a newer record leaves the newer record intact
invalid code-exchange response persists nothing; invalid refresh response persists only a valid rotated refresh token; no in-flight/refreshing state remains; returns provider_failed
retry can acquire with current client credentials without any human-login outcome
delivery/credential/challenge paths return interaction_required without creating a pending login; only explicit prepare creates one
pending login lifetime is host-configured and bounded (default 10 minutes), fixed at creation and survives the creating prepare's deadline or cancellation
by default a pending login lives in the creating process, which receives its callback on its own listener and completes it by state
when the host opts to persist pending logins, another process sharing the store completes one by state (paste flow); the PKCE verifier stays only in the pending record, never in metadata or logs
two prepares for one grant key create two pending logins keyed by state, each with its own redirect and client; each callback completes only its own login

a pending login beyond the host-configurable cap (default 5) for one grant key, per process or per store when persisted, cancels the oldest, atomically in a persisted store; expired pending logins are deleted
completing one pending login leaves the others valid; each completion replaces the grant's client and tokens, so the newest completed login wins
a pending login ends exactly once by completion, cancel (including by the cap) or expiry; later callbacks for it fail interaction_required
nonidentity metadata, token-endpoint auth method and runtime secret changes do not permanently fail stored session or persist secret
widening the allowed ceiling finds the existing grant; effective scopes are granted scopes intersected with the current ceiling at use
narrowing the ceiling hides scopes at use only; after a refresh under the narrow ceiling and widening it again the scope is still available
only a Bearer 403 insufficient_scope creates a step-up requirement (Ch) for the challenged operation; a 401 or any other 403 never does
a challenge requirement is not persisted on the binding; later operations use the stored grant, including scopes added by step-up consent
step-up or re-acquisition requests previously granted plus new ceiling-filtered scopes and records response scopes within previously granted plus acquisition ceiling; earlier scopes are not lost

interaction_required carries the full required set R = H ∪ E ∪ Ch, deduplicated and byte-sorted; the host passes it to prepare as explicit required scopes and consent includes them; every scoped access_denied also carries R
prepare with explicit required scopes outside the caller's ceiling fails access_denied carrying R before any network I/O
401 or Bearer 403 insufficient_scope on hooks/intercept, hooks/configuration or hooks/capabilities replays once with the same request id and body; second rejection fails
explicit trusted preset uses issuer metadata and does not require PRM
independently approved event/upload bindings share consent only with same explicit grant partition

an invalid or unparseable callback (redirect or its own query, state, iss, fragment, userinfo, missing code, both code and error, duplicated parameter) fails access_denied with login_ended false and does not consume the login; authorization-server-added parameters such as session_state are accepted
literal IPv4/IPv6 loopback HTTP redirect accepted; remote HTTP rejected
each login may bind a new loopback port; authorization, DCR and token requests and callback validation use that login's exact redirect including the port
a host-declared CIMD redirect_uris entry without a port, or with another port, matches a loopback http redirect without userinfo on any port; localhost is never accepted
initial request read+write grants read; refresh with no scope stays read and cannot fabricate write
insufficient_scope without scope uses H ∪ E when non-empty, otherwise fails access_denied with no scopes; it never invents permissions
initial read+write request grants read; refresh response scoped read write records read only, persists rotated refresh and stays usable; a write-requiring operation fails access_denied
response scopes outside the allowed ceiling (e.g. openid, offline_access) are dropped from the recorded grant, not an error

with every source available the SDK selects a pre-registered client, else CIMD (PKCE, client_id_metadata_document_supported true), else permitted DCR with registration_endpoint, else credential_unavailable

a host-supplied pre-registered client is used even when CIMD and DCR are available; adding one later makes a recorded CIMD/DCR selection obsolete, selecting a new grant key whose old tokens are never presented under the new client
PKCE with a configured CIMD URL and client_id_metadata_document_supported true sends the URL as client_id with no client secret, token auth none and no stored registration record
absent or non-true client_id_metadata_document_supported skips CIMD and uses permitted DCR
a redirect matching no host-declared CIMD redirect_uris entry (loopback compared without port) fails invalid_configuration before any pending login
no SDK network request targets the CIMD URL or a URL derived from it
client_credentials never uses CIMD; it uses a pre-registered client or DCR with a secret-based method
invalid_client for a CIMD client is invalid_configuration and never triggers DCR for that operation
registration_endpoint advertised but host policy does not permit the exact issuer: no registration request; credential_unavailable
non-HTTPS, destination-policy-refused or redirecting registration endpoint sends no further request and fails untrusted_destination

only host prepare registers a PKCE client, inside the prepare that creates the pending login, with that login's exact redirect and application_type native for loopback; each new login registers anew; lookup and delivery never register

completion commits the issued client_id with the tokens into the grant record under the dcr client identity; a re-registered client replaces it without changing the grant key; refresh uses the stored client

invalid_client at PKCE completion ends only that pending login (the stored grant is kept); at refresh it returns interaction_required and compare-and-deletes the grant only if it still holds the presented client_id and refresh token
client-credentials registration: concurrent processes register once under the registration-key lock; a compare-and-set loser deletes its secret reference and uses the winner's record
a client-credentials registration record is reused by every client-credentials grant with the same namespace and issuer

a passed nonzero client_secret_expires_at or unresolvable secret reference makes the record unusable; client-credentials acquisition, including the up-front lookup, re-registers under coordination before any token-endpoint request

client credentials: token-endpoint invalid_client compare-and-deletes that registration generation, re-registers at most once and re-acquires once; a repeated invalid_client is credential_unavailable; no metadata refetch
the client secret is written only through the host secret-storage hook; registration, binding, grant and pending-login records and errors never contain it
without a host secret-storage hook a client-credentials DCR fails credential_unavailable with no registration request; PKCE DCR is unaffected
newly advertised CIMD support or a removed registration_endpoint does not move a working grant off its recorded client
registration_access_token and registration_client_uri are ignored, never persisted and never used
a host initial access token configured for one exact issuer is sent only to that issuer's registration endpoint, never to another issuer's, and never persisted
the up-front lookup never registers a PKCE client and returns interaction_required; for client credentials it may register when no usable record exists, subject to the backoff
a 2xx JSON registration response failing validation (secret for PKCE, replaced redirect, swapped auth method) persists nothing and returns invalid_configuration, not retry

after a registration record is replaced or compare-and-deleted, the old secret reference is deleted through the host hook once the compare-and-set succeeds; a losing compare-and-set deletes only its own fresh reference

after a failed client-credentials registration, no registration request is sent for that key until the backoff (default 1 minute doubling, capped at 1 hour) passes, shared through a shared store; meanwhile the last failure's code is returned (provider_failed for retryable failures); host prepare bypasses it
a registration response with Retry-After sets the next attempt no earlier than Retry-After and no earlier than the exponential backoff, capped at the host maximum

discovery answered 401 with no usable grant skips the backend and emits a host-visible diagnostic {backendId, code configuration_unavailable, authError interaction_required, recovery login}; no credentials or bodies; cancellation emits no diagnostic and propagates
after a successful host prepare for the skipped backend's event endpoint, the next event admission re-attempts discovery without waiting for backoff and admits the backend's routes

a configuration_unavailable skip with no authError, or with recovery retry, is re-attempted only at the first admission or initialize after backoff (30s, doubling, capped at 1h, host-configurable); earlier admissions do not contact the backend

a configuration_unavailable skip whose recovery is login, configure or none is not re-attempted when backoff elapses; only a successful host prepare for that backend's endpoint or reinitialization re-attempts it
configuration_invalid, no_applicable_subscriptions and configuration_local_secret skips are never re-attempted before reinitialization, even after prepare or backoff elapses
a retry runs inside the single shared admission: concurrent callers observe old or complete new routes, never partial; events admitted before the retry succeeded are not replayed

omitted preset scopes are no constraint; present ones must equal the client's configured scopes (else invalid_configuration); they are requested, never required, and never appear in R or any error's scope set unless host-required

R outside the ceiling, including a host-required scope, fails access_denied carrying R on every entry point; with a stored binding or explicit preset there is no network I/O; an unbound target (an anonymous request answered by 401) runs at most one protected-resource discovery (one request to a usable resource_metadata, else at most the path-specific and origin-root well-known locations) and no authorization-server request
configured requested scopes (and so a preset's scopes) outside the ceiling fail invalid_configuration as an SDK auth error, never a native exception, provider_failed or a silent drop

a 401 retires the sent generation, if current, before every other decision step and whatever the outcome (including a malformed challenge); its in-ceiling scope hint is used only by a client-credentials acquisition in the same operation, never stored, never added to R and never yields access_denied

a bad auth-param, two Bearer challenges, a duplicated parameter or a malformed scope (empty, tab, repeated, leading or trailing space, invalid character) fails access_denied with no scopes; a 403 that is not insufficient_scope is access_denied and not an auth retry

403 insufficient_scope when the sent generation (or no token) is current and its grant covers R within the ceiling fails access_denied carrying R without replaying the token or creating a login; a newer current generation that covers R is used instead

complete() persists the grant, then fails access_denied carrying the pending login's stored R when granted ∩ current ceiling does not cover it; a pending record without stored R uses its prepare-time H, else the current H
a refresh or client-credentials grant narrower than R fails access_denied carrying R with the grant persisted
scopes are attached only by decide and complete step 7; errors from host callbacks, stores, the network and the token endpoint carry none, and login_ended appears only on complete() errors

every complete() error carries login_ended: state lookup runs before any host callback (absent, unknown, expired or ended state: interaction_required/true); invalid callback, including a handle naming another login than the live state, access_denied/false with both logins pending; login_ended always describes the login named by state; pre-claim host policy keeps its code (client source no longer permitted: invalid_configuration)/false; an uncertain claim re-reads the store (gone: true, otherwise false); after the claim every error is /true

every entry point that yields a credential or handles a challenge (credential/delivery, prepare, challenge, preemptive credential paths, legacy provider adapters) produces decide's outcome; the routing test lists them
the transport hands every 401 to the provider, a 403 only when it parses as exactly one Bearer insufficient_scope challenge, and returns any other 403 without a retry
a token rejected on the challenged replay is handed to the provider, so a 401 retires it

after the claim invalid_grant is interaction_required; invalid_client is credential_unavailable (pre-registered), invalid_configuration (CIMD) or interaction_required (DCR); every other token-endpoint error, an unreachable or 404 endpoint and an invalid response are provider_failed; none carry scopes

refresh and client-credentials token-endpoint errors: PKCE refresh invalid_grant is refresh_rejected, client-credentials invalid_grant and unauthorized_client are credential_unavailable, invalid_client maps by client source (a client-credentials DCR client re-registers once), every other error is provider_failed; none carry scopes
